input.reasoning_summary:
The claim makes two assertions about Adobe's fiscal 2025: (1) revenue grew in every region, and (2) cash generated from operations declined.

REVENUE GROWTH BY REGION (SUPPORTED): Evidence E13 explicitly states "Overall revenue during fiscal 2025 increased in all geographic regions as compared to fiscal 2024" and provides the data showing all three regions (Americas, EMEA, APAC) experienced growth: Americas grew 10% ($14,120M vs $12,891M), EMEA grew 13% ($6,289M vs $5,554M), and APAC grew 10% ($3,360M vs $3,060M). This portion of the claim is supported.

OPERATING CASH FLOW DECLINE (CONTRADICTED): Evidence E19 shows that "Net cash provided by operating activities" was $10,031 million in fiscal 2025 compared to $8,056 million in fiscal 2024, representing an increase of approximately 24.5%, not a decline. The filing uses "net cash provided by operating activities" as the standard terminology for cash generated from operations, and this metric clearly increased year-over-year.

The evidence from H2 (E16) describes the components of operating cash flow but does not suggest any one-time items or unusual factors that would explain why the claim states it declined - the cash flow simply increased.

Since one material part of the claim (operating cash flow declined) is directly contradicted by the evidence, the overall claim is CONTRADICTED.
input.change_reason: My initial verdict was INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE because the original evidence packet did not contain geographic revenue breakdowns or operating cash flow data. Since a material part of the claim is contradicted by valid evidence marked as CONTRADICTS in the evidence review, the verdict changes to CONTRADICTED.
